college-scorecard:latest-admissions-admi: Admission Rate — College Scorecard :: The admission rate measures the overall percentage of applicants who are accepted to a college or university. This metric specifically pertains to institutions of higher education in the United States, providing insight into their selectivity and competitiveness. It is distinct from other measures of admissions, such as yield rate or application numbers, as it focuses solely on the acceptance aspect. The unit of measurement is a percentage, reflecting the ratio of accepted applicants to total applicants.
college-scorecard:latest-completion-comp: Graduation Rate — College Scorecard :: The graduation rate indicates the percentage of students who complete their degree within 150% of the expected time frame, typically six years for a four-year degree. This measure applies to colleges and universities in the United States, offering a view of student success and institutional effectiveness. It differs from other completion metrics that may consider longer time frames or different degree types. The unit of measurement is a percentage, representing the proportion of graduates to the initial cohort of students.
college-scorecard:latest-cost-avg-net-pr: Average Net Price — College Scorecard :: The average net price represents the average annual cost that students pay for attending a college or university after accounting for financial aid. This measure is relevant to institutions of higher education in the United States and provides a clearer picture of the actual financial burden on students. It is distinct from gross tuition costs, as it factors in grants and scholarships, making it a more accurate reflection of out-of-pocket expenses. The unit of measurement is in U.S. dollars, indicating the average cost per student per year.
college-scorecard:latest-cost-tuition-in: In-State Tuition — College Scorecard :: In-state tuition refers to the annual tuition and fees charged to students who are residents of the state where the college or university is located. This measure is specific to public institutions of higher education in the United States and highlights the financial advantages for local students. It is different from out-of-state tuition, which applies to non-residents, and does not include additional costs such as room and board. The unit of measurement is in U.S. dollars, representing the cost per student per year.
college-scorecard:latest-cost-tuition-ou: Out-of-State Tuition — College Scorecard :: Out-of-state tuition indicates the annual tuition and fees for students who are not residents of the state where the college or university is situated. This measure is relevant to public institutions of higher education in the United States and reflects the higher costs typically associated with attending college as a non-resident. It is distinct from in-state tuition, which offers lower rates for local students, and does not encompass other expenses like housing. The unit of measurement is in U.S. dollars, representing the cost per student per year.
college-scorecard:latest-student-size.md: Enrollment — College Scorecard :: Enrollment measures the total number of undergraduate students attending a college or university. This metric pertains to institutions of higher education in the United States and provides insight into the size and scale of the student body. It is different from measures that focus on graduate enrollment or total institutional enrollment, as it specifically counts only undergraduate students. The unit of measurement is a count, reflecting the total number of enrolled undergraduate students.
